Preserve referenced identities, costumes and rigid handmade masks; eye openings and mask edges never deform. All humans wear their referenced masks. Zahhak keeps his established support hand, weaker-leg side and exact reference snake count: natural single-headed black snakes remain independently alive in every visible shot. Panic accelerates his uneven attempts, never cures his limp. Camera is a frightened witness beside Zahhak: close handheld, body-driven recoil, obstructed frames, searching pans and short focus losses followed by recovery of the essential action. Each cut changes physical viewpoint, height or lens; no digital crop pretending to be a new shot. Other people are seen from his viewing position or the explicitly described reverse. No smooth gimbal, unmotivated orbit, zoom, or static portrait. Only a shot explicitly marked LOCKED may stop moving. World directions stay fixed; screen positions belong to each stated angle. Masks stay attached when heads turn; a full backward look requires a torso pivot.

FIXED SPACE

One immense PRIVATE ROYAL BEDCHAMBER, not a throne hall. NORTH: a raised platform with a luxurious burgundy Persian-textile BED, reached by one broad step. A level main floor runs 12 meters SOUTH from that platform to the NORTH stairs of a roughly six-meter-square sunken seating area. Exactly THREE broad shallow steps descend SOUTH into this lower square. The lower floor has thick carpets and perimeter cushions with clear standing/walking space; a narrow exposed stone strip borders the central carpet. Massive columns, bronze objects and cabinets surround the MAIN floor. EAST/WEST entrances near the NORTH bed zone connect to dark corridors. All real companions may move on the main floor and rim, never down onto ANY recess step or lower floor. Only Zahhak and named dream/prophecy bodies occupy the lower square. No extra people.

PLAN 03 | LIGHT AND EXPOSURE

DEEP NIGHT. Blackness is the dominant image, not a blue-lit room. The ONLY source is one fixed vertical cold silver-blue shaft through a small ceiling opening directly above the CENTER OF THE SUNKEN SQUARE. It lands on one isolated circular patch of the LOWER floor. Its edge is sharply contained; faint airborne dust describes the shaft only inside it. Surrounding air remains black and clear, without room-filling haze. The beam never follows a person or changes position with the camera.

The bedroom keeps its full architecture and three levels, but most walls, columns, cabinets, bronze objects, bed textiles, upper floor and doorways disappear completely. All lamps stay unlit. No daylight, window light, corridor spill, face key, fill, additional rim light or second spotlight. The lit carpet is a receiving surface, never an emissive floor: dark textiles absorb light, allowing only extremely weak localized bounce outside the patch. Do not brighten the set merely to explain the geography.

At close range, reveal a fragment at a time: one visible eye through a rigid mask opening, a narrow mask plane, a knuckle, a cloth fold or one moving snake glint. Never evenly expose the whole face or body. A turn can take that fragment back into black. Highlights belong to fixed world-space light, not the lens; no permanent eye catchlight, luminous eyes or light that tracks a face. Keep masks and skin unchanged. Emotional action stays legible through these fragments, movement and breath.

Expose for the lit patch without clipping it; lock exposure and black level through every cut and focus change. Close-ups and reverse angles receive no compensating light. Preserve large areas of true black without shadow recovery or a uniform blue wash; only sparse highlights carry restrained silver-blue color. Dream and prophecy figures never reveal identifying facial planes, mask details or eyes, including in low angles. Their silhouettes come from the existing shaft or lit floor behind them, never a new backlight. No aura, energy effects or glowing outlines.

Character and location references control identity and construction, not their photographed brightness. The written lighting overrides any brighter reference. In the dream layer, three bodies stand tightly shoulder-to-shoulder at SOUTH boundary of the central light: Fereydun center, Warrior LEFT at his EAST side, Warrior RIGHT at WEST. 35mm from NORTHWEST close to Zahhak, looking southeast into his front-three-quarter mask as he looks past the lens toward P1 above NORTH. He lifts a trembling free hand as if to begin an explanation, aborts it, swallows and bends forward. Camera sinks with his breath; no intelligible dialogue.

SHOT 03-02 | 03–06s | THE WAITING EYES

28mm over Zahhak's SOUTH shoulder looking NORTH/up. P1 and Arnavaz appear in one crowded upper edge, bodies angled down toward him; Guard A is partly hidden behind P1. Whip between their uncertain eyes while retaining Zahhak's shoulder foreground. Nobody steps down; their silence pressures him.

24mm at his WEST flank. He turns his body SOUTH, planting the staff before pivoting, and makes a short distressed gesture toward the lower center. SHOT 03-04 | 09–12s | THE COMPACT SHAPE

Continue direction after a hard cut to 28mm at Zahhak's NORTHWEST shoulder. Slide just 20 centimeters sideways to uncover the three closely packed silhouettes SOUTH beyond the moonlit pool. Expose for the silver carpet, not faces. The bright floor/beam beside them separates their outline; there is no rear lamp or facial fill.

LIGHTING: Keep the trio nearly solid black against the existing patch and thin shaft. Separate their outer contours only where a real background contrast permits it; faces, eyes and identifying mask details remain completely unreadable.

PLAN 03 | TIMED SHOTS AND HANDOFF

SHOT 03-05 | 12–14s | THE EYE REFUSES

65mm from WEST close to Zahhak's right eye opening as he faces SOUTH. His gaze fixes ahead, then flicks between three dark heights. The mask remains immovable on his face. One snake slides across his collar and he barely notices. Handheld tremor breaks the clean eye composition.

LIGHTING: One eye is barely visible through the fixed opening; the surrounding mask and head dissolve into black. A passing scale catches a brief trace, never a luminous snake or permanent catchlight.

35mm over his NORTHWEST shoulder, a small lateral searching move. Find three separate shoulder contours inside the compact shape: central slightly forward, two taller flanking. A hand edge and a low mace contour catch spill; every face and identifying mask detail remain black. They neither spread nor attack yet.

LIGHTING: Reveal three shoulder contours in the darkness, not three lit portraits. Only a small hand edge and low mace outline take spill. Their upper bodies remain largely merged and their faces never separate from black.

SHOT 03-07 | 17–20s | THE BODY BELIEVES

24mm beside Zahhak's WEST shoulder at chest height. He takes one unsupported-looking half-step back, immediately catches his weight on the staff and raises his free palm toward the shapes. Camera recoils with him, recovers the staff hand after a short focus miss. Stop before any change of the warriors' formation.

END STATE AND EDIT

Zahhak remains NORTH half of lower square facing SOUTH, one pace inside the stair foot, staff supporting him. Three warriors remain tightly grouped SOUTH at the light boundary, facing him, faces unseen. All seven real companions hold their upper-rim marks, hidden by framing and darkness, never absent or below.

SOUND

Zahhak's broken breathing; an aborted wordless vocalization; fabric tightening; small staff impacts. The three figures contribute only faint clothing movement. No reveal sting or supernatural sound.
